title: Bayard to Montmorency
correspondents: Bayard → Montmorency
shelfmark: BnF, Clairambault 325, f.84
status: Attempted, open (22 Sept 2026, targets/bayard1526/): 17th-c. copy; 56 signs of 29 kinds transcribed. Printed in Champollion-Figeac 1847 (CCXVIII) with the cipher omitted. Calvimont and Raince 1526 keys do not fit; too short blind. Needs the original (V. 41 f. 4).
why: Ciphered letter of Bayard to Montmorency, 5 Jan 1526; what the cipher hides is not known.

title: Murberg, Johan, Görtz, Georg Heinrich von to unknown recipient
correspondents: Murberg, Johan, Görtz, Georg Heinrich von → unknown recipient
shelfmark: National Library of Sweden
status: DECODE R4350: Non-decrypted. Viewed 22 Sept 2026: the record is the whole Murberg volume (KB I.g.18, 114 images); the cipher is five passages (809 numeric groups 1-848, 175 distinct) inside a German peace memorandum of 1717 on Poland, the Czar and Norway (PDF pp. 34-41). No decipherment on the pages; the only Görtz key on DECODE (R7691, BL Add MS 32287 f.2, 1716) is a French 4-digit code, not this one. Ciphertext-only annealing (homophonic letter, alphabetical syllabary) failed, and failed its synthetic control. Needs Görtz's German chancery key (Riksarkivet Görtz papers). See targets/goertz1717/.
why: Ciphered letter of Murberg, Johan, Görtz, Georg Heinrich von to unknown recipient, 1717; what the cipher hides is not known.

title: Riksarkivet key-box and Oxenstierna ciphers, 8 records (Bremen 1631, R4282, R4306 and Rusdorff 1625 read or partly read and removed)
correspondents: unknown → Camerarius?, Amsterdam; Rusdorff → Oxenstierna; Swedish agent → Oxenstierna
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, TNA of Sweden (8 items)
status: DECODE R4284–R4341, 8 records in four different ciphers, each its own entry since the one-key split of 14 Oct 2026. Viewed 21 Sept 2026. The two Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330–R4331, riksarkivet1628.html) are read and removed from this entry; R4282 was deciphered by George Lasry (decode4282.html). R4306: contributed partial Dutch decipherment by George Lasry, transcribed with CTTS then solved with Opus 5.5 (17 Oct 2026; sweden4306.html, which also records this project's failed attempt of 21 Sept 2026); pencilled 1632? and Amsterdam attribution remain qualified, four code identities open. R4336–R4337 turned out to be Rusdorff's London letters of February 1625 in a homophonic cipher with an alphabetical nomenclator; key recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry (21 Oct 2026, PR #72; rusdorff1625.html) and removed from this entry. Open: R4284 (Latin 1628, Camerarius docket; riksarkivet4284.html) — attacked with Latin annealing and against two box keys, not broken; R4333–R4335 (Rusdorff → Oxenstierna 1628, another cipher; rusdorff1628.html) and R4338–R4341 (E 708, Swedish, June 1633, not 1646; glossed in part at the time; oxenstierna1633.html) surveyed only.
why: One remaining key-box ciphertext that resisted a first attack, and Oxenstierna correspondence of 1628 and 1633 with a key collection that may hold their keys.

title: Frederik Gijsbert van Dedem tot de Gelder (Constantinople) to Maarten van der Goes, No. XVIII "Duplicaat", 26 Aug 1799 (R1895)
correspondents: Frederik Gijsbert van Dedem tot de Gelder (1743-1820) → Maarten van der Goes (1751-1826)
shelfmark: NA The Hague, 2.01.08 (Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken, 1796-1810) inv. 346
status: Narrowed 23 Oct 2026 to R1895. R2120 (22 Dec 1788) was read at the time (its decipherment is R2121); R2122 (15 Jan 1789) and R2131 (9 Feb 1793) were read on 23 Oct 2026 with the legation codebook filed under Kroll, NA 1.02.20 inv. 785 (targets/dedem1788/, dedem1788.html), and leave the catalogue. title: Willem Frederik Roell (1767-1829), minister of Foreign Affairs (Amsterdam) to Frederik Gijsbertvan Dedem tot de Gelder (1743-1820), 2 ciphertexts
correspondents: Willem Frederik Roell (1767-1829), minister of Foreign Affairs → Frederik Gijsbertvan Dedem tot de Gelder (1743-1820)
shelfmark: NA The Hague, legatie Turkije, inv.nr. 804 (2 items)
status: DECODE R1469-R1470 viewed 21 Sept 2026 (targets/roell1809/). 13 pages of code throughout, unaddressed and unsigned; no decipherment on the scans. 2,585 groups (931 distinct) to about 3,300, heavily homophonic (no group above ~1%), not alphabetical. Not the 1788-93 Dedem code (overlap at chance), nor the Spaen 1808 or Fagel 1804 codes. No DECODE key; Roell's papers (NA 2.21.008.78) list letters from Dedem and from S. F. Croiset 1808-09 but no codebook. Not breakable without the key or a crib.
why: Ciphered despatches of Willem Frederik Roell (1767-1829), minister of Foreign Affairs to Frederik Gijsbertvan Dedem tot de Gelder (1743-1820), 9 Feb 1809; what the cipher hides is not known.

title: Transylvanian cipher letters, Keresdi Bethlen and Kemény collections
correspondents: unknown → unknown (Transylvania)
shelfmark: Romanian National Archives, Cluj: Keresdi Bethlen 14–15, Kemény XIX
status: Checked 22 Sept 2026: DECODE R4933-R4942 are N/A with no decryption attached, and no published reading was found; the collection is at the Romanian National Archives in Cluj, not Sibiu. Split by system 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry). Narrowed 23 Oct 2026: R4937, R4940 and R4942 read with the Bethlen family key recovered ciphertext-only, and R4939 broken ciphertext-only in its own key and read (targets/transylvania1645/, transylvania1645.html); they leave the catalogue. Still open: R4936 (decoded with the family key, not read: g/q look-alikes the 1,704-px scan cannot separate), R4938 (three short spans decoded, one word unread), R4941 (a different substitution, targets/r4941/) and the Kemény XIX records R4933-R4935 (targets/kemeny1628/).
why: Transylvania under George I Rákóczi, around the peace of Linz (1645).

title: Aphra Behn (Astrea) → James Halsall / Thomas Killigrew, Antwerp spy letters with undecoded numeric cipher words
correspondents: Aphra Behn (with William Scot's intelligence) → James Halsall; → Thomas Killigrew
folio_note: 9 letters. EMLO says the numeric cipher words are not decoded in SP 29/169 f. 155 (31 Aug) and SP 29/172 f. 15 (17 Sept, to Killigrew); others are decoded interlinear; SP 29/169 f. 47 postscript gives the key to her symbol cipher.
status: EMLO (Behn catalogue): 'The letter contains limited instances of a simple substitutional numeric cipher ... This is not decoded' (31 Aug) and 'a few instances ... that are not decoded' (17 Sept). Sibling letters are decoded interline, so the numeric code can be rebuilt. Not in the repo (known.py: Behn, Halsall no hit). 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): printed with decipherment in the Taylor Editions (Oxford 2025). Correction: SP 29/172 f. 16r has 82 ships, not 62.
why: Fills the few code words left in Aphra Behn's 1666 espionage letters, a much-studied episode.

title: Thomas Harrison and William Jephson → Henry Cromwell, letters partly in numeric cipher, partly decoded
correspondents: Major-General Thomas Harrison; William Jephson → Henry Cromwell
shelfmark: British Library, Lansdowne MS 821, fols 154-155, 170-171, 290-291, 350-351 (and one more, folio not given)
folio_note: 5 letters; Lansdowne MS 823 ff. 339-340 is a draft code between Henry Cromwell and Lord Broghill (key lead).
status: EMLO (Henry Cromwell catalogue): 'The letter is written in part in a substitutional numeric cipher. It has been transcribed in code ... and attempts at decoding have been made in the footnotes' — i.e. partial decoding only. Not in the repo (known.py: Lansdowne 821 no hit).
why: Jephson was Cromwell's envoy to Charles X of Sweden in 1657; cipher parts carry the diplomatic substance.

title: Comenius → Andreas Klobusiczky, cipher passage of 24 May 1655 (Rákóczi archive)
correspondents: Jan Amos Komenský (Comenius) → Andreas Klobusiczky (Rákóczi's councillor)
shelfmark: Magyar Nemzeti Levéltár Országos Levéltár (Budapest), E 190 (Archivum familiae Rákóczi): 5.t. 788 ff. 389-390v; 6962 ff. 351-354v; 5.t. 800 ff. 414-415v
folio_note: One passage of 50 letters and the numbers 7, 865, 73 inside news quoted from an English correspondent; printed MHH XXIII (1874) no. CIII p. 178 and Patera 1892 no. CLII p. 178 (italic). The 4 Aug 1655 sentence is deciphered (write-up comenius1655); 22 Jul and 6 Sept have invisible ink / secret script printed in clear by Szilágyi 1890.
status: 4 Aug 1655 sentence deciphered in print (Szilágyi 1890 p. 393; Patera 1892 p. 182); key = Rákóczi envoys' table, MHH XXIII p. 740. The 24 May passage does not decipher with that table, shifts, keyword ciphers, or as a simple substitution of Latin (annealing with matched control); no decipherment in MHH, Szilágyi 1890 or Patera. See targets/comenius1655/.
why: Comenius's secret line to George II Rákóczi on the Swedish-Polish war of 1655, when he pressed Transylvania to join Sweden.

title: Duke Augustus of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel (Gustavus Selenus) → Athanasius Kircher, enclosed cryptogram
correspondents: August the Younger, Duke of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel → Athanasius Kircher
shelfmark: Archivio della Pontificia Università Gregoriana, APUG 563, fols 88r-89v (letter, manifestation note 'Cipher') and fols 179r-181v ('Cryptogram')
folio_note: letter plus a cryptogram of 3 leaves
status: EMLO (Kircher catalogue) keywords 'steganography; cryptography; ciphers', manifestation notes 'Cipher' and 'Cryptogram'. Context: Kircher's Polygraphia nova (1663); the duke wrote the Cryptomenytices (1624) as Gustavus Selenus. Whether the cryptogram is a test message with its solution is not stated.
why: A cipher challenge between the two leading cryptographic authors of the 1660s.

correspondents: Cardinal of Sigüenza → Antoine Perrenot de Granvelle
shelfmark: Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional de España, BDH bdh0000172763
status: BNE catalogue: six letters dated in Naples between April and June 1554, partly ciphered. No decipherment mentioned. Not on DECODE, not in the repo. Neighbouring Granvelle-family ciphers PP1/PP3 (Pich-Ponce 2023) may apply; bne_hispana README notes a Gonzaga sibling (bdh0000172697) with decipherment as crib.

title: Ferdinand II of Aragon → his father John II: letter from Hostalric with cipher passages and interlinear notes
correspondents: Ferdinand the Catholic → John II of Aragon
shelfmark: Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional de España, BDH bdh0000186643
folio_note: one letter; 'Notas interlineales con parte de la cifra, de diferente mano'
status: BNE catalogue: autograph signature, remains of a plaque seal, interlinear notes 'with part of the cipher' in a different hand, so a contemporary partial decipherment sits on the letter. Not on DECODE, not in the repo. Checked 28 Oct 2026: Verified 28 Oct: no published reading found; interlinear partial decipherment per BNE catalogue (not seen). 1473 would be among the oldest ciphers in the catalogue.

title: Frederick V (Winter King) → Johann Joachim von Rusdorf: French letter with enciphered names
correspondents: Frederick V of the Palatinate → Johann Joachim von Rusdorf
shelfmark: Heidelberg University Library, Urkunde Lehmann 5918 (Manuscriptorium HUL___URKLEHMANN5918PWTN4)
folio_note: one letter; the record: 'mit den verschlüsselten Namen' (names enciphered)
status: Heidelberg description: French letter with the names enciphered. Probably a name code in an otherwise clear letter, possibly short. Rusdorf's ciphers for Oxenstierna are in the repo (rusdorff1625, rusdorff1628), but this is a different correspondence.
why: Palatine exile correspondence with a Rusdorf name code; Rusdorf's other ciphers have been broken here, so the nomenclator may carry over.

correspondents: Landgrave Moritz, Johann Popp and others
shelfmark: Kassel, Universitätsbibliothek, 2° Ms. theol. 181 (former cover, Bl. 1/2); Popp letters in 2° Ms. chem. 19[2 and 19[5
folio_note: the pieces in cipher are 'teilweise veröffentlicht' by R. Schmitz / A. Winkelmann, Pharmazeutische Zeitung 106 (1961), pp. 374-378

title: German Foreign Office → Bernstorff (Washington), German cipher telegram forwarded through the US Embassy Berlin (Grew), text not printed in FRUS
correspondents: German Foreign Office → Count Bernstorff, German ambassador at Washington (via Chargé Joseph C. Grew → Secretary of State)
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, 1910-29 decimal file (World War I series; FRUS 1916 Supplement doc. 424)
folio_note: FRUS prints only Grew's covering telegram: '[German cipher. Not printed.]'
status: FRUS 1916 Supplement, The World War, doc. 424: Grew forwards 'the following cipher telegram which is said to relate to' the Washington talks; the German code text is omitted. German diplomatic traffic sent over the US channel in 1916-17 was in codes 13040/0075 and was largely read by Room 40, so a decrypt may exist in TNA (HW 7, ADM 223); not checked.
why: German code text passed by the State Department during the 1916 peace-note period; checkable against the Room 40 codebooks reconstructed for 13040.

correspondents: Gilbert Guillouet d'Orvilliers; Lemoyne → secretary of state for the Navy

status: ANOM inventory: 'Lettre en majeure partie chiffrée'; 'Passages chiffrés non traduits'; no transcription noted. 27 Oct 2026 (targets/orvilliers1759/): attempted; all 227 notices of the d'Orvilliers branch of COL C14 swept; 36 items with cipher, none with a digital object online although ANOM flags them "document numérisé". Order images from ANOM.
why: Defence and famine in French Guiana during the Seven Years' War.
